title: Coalescer oncall playbook and weekly sync - 2026-09-14
content:
Purpose:
This note captures our weekly sync on the coalescer/kv-batch coordinator work, a lightweight oncall playbook draft for common incidents, recent experiment outcomes, and prioritized action items for the next two sprints. Intention is to have this be the canonical working doc for triage and runbook edits before we move the playbook to Confluence.

Attendees:
- Aisha Kapoor (notes, lead)
- Evan Park (kernel/low-level batching)
- Lina Chen (coalescer service owner)
- Samuel Ortiz (SRE / observability)
- Priya Nair (perf + bench)
- Guests: Mikhail (solutions eng, customer impact)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Coalescer staging A saw a 12% p95 token latency reduction for small-seq (<=64) synthetic traces after applying adaptive puncturing and heuristic-based prefill cutoff.
- Two recurring oncall incidents last week were caused by: (1) a race in the coordinator backoff window when under extreme burst (>5k rps short spikes), and (2) an eviction thrash loop when the KV prefill index compaction ran concurrently with a large model switch.
- We drafted an oncall playbook covering immediate mitigation steps, how to hotfix the coordinator, and escalation paths to kernel team.

Notes / discussion points:
1) Incident root causes (recap)
   - Burst race: coordinator backoff logic used a per-shard randomized delay but didn't account for global token budget updates; that allowed many shards to retry simultaneously after a budget refill, producing a transient overload on the batcher.
   - Compaction thrash: compaction job was scheduled on the same node as the serving worker in a small-capacity pool; compaction I/O caused CPU steal and KV eviction patterns that then increased miss rate and prefills.

2) Recent experiment (A/B) - adaptive puncturing + prefill cutoff
   - Hypothesis: for small sequence workloads, puncturing (temporarily breaking large micro-batches to serve small seqs) will improve tail latency without harming throughput materially.
   - Setup: 10k synthetic connections, mixed seq lengths (80% <=64, 20% long), run over 6 hours during off-peak on staging-a.
   - Result: p95 token latency down 12%, p99 down 6%, overall throughput down 0.8% (within noise). CPU utilization increased ~3% on batch worker nodes.
   - Notes: improvement magnified for traffic with high short-seq ratio (>=70%).

3) Kernel interaction notes
   - Evan: kernel preemption path needs a small API to accept "puncture hints" from coalescer; this will let the kernel prioritize small requests without a full batch tear-down. Draft PR created (linked).
   - Action: add a lightweight protobuf flag to request header (puncture_preference: LOW|MED|HIGH) and a fast-path in scheduler to check it. Target: PR by 2026-09-22.

4) Oncall playbook (draft) - quick reference for the coalescer and KV-batching incidents:
   - Symptoms to watch:
     * sudden jump in small-seq p95 with no corresponding increase in overall rps
     * rapid increase in KV eviction rate (>5% minute-over-minute)
     * coordinator queue depth spikes with many "retry" logs around the same timestamp
   - Immediate mitigations (order matters):
     1) Flip staging override to apply conservative puncturing: POST /admin/coalescer/override {"puncture_mode":"conservative"} (rollout 20% nodes -> 100% in 3 mins).
     2) Disable compaction on suspect nodes: kubectl annotate node/<node> coalescer.compaction=disabled; restart compaction-controller on the node pool.
     3) Apply coordinator backoff hotfix (see hotfix steps below) if retry storms continue.
   - Hotfix steps for coordinator backoff race:
     * Checkout: git checkout -b hotfix/coordinator-backoff-9821 && git cherry-pick <commit-id>
     * Merge to hotfix branch, CI smoke on canary, then rollout to non-prod pools only.
     * If rollout causes increased latency, rollback immediately: kubectl rollout undo deployment/coalescer-service --to-revision=<previous>.
   - Escalation matrix:
     * If after mitigations tail latency still > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes, page eng-serving-runtime oncall (pager id in internal runbook).
     * If KV eviction rate correlates with compaction, page infra-storage (Samuel) and consider moving compaction jobs to a dedicated cluster.

5) Observability gaps we should fill
   - Add a per-shard global backoff heartbeat metric (coalescer.shard.backoff.heartbeat) to detect synchronized retries.
   - Instrument coordinator to emit token-budget-change events with timestamp and origin (autoscaler, manual refill, fallback).
   - Add a composite alert that ties together: coordinator.retry_rate spikes + batch_worker_queue_depth > 90th percentile + kv_eviction_rate > 3%.

6) Prioritized action items (owners and target dates)
   - Aisha: finalize oncall playbook and move to Confluence with runbook links (target 2026-09-20).
   - Evan: open PR for puncture_preference header and kernel fast-path (target 2026-09-22). Linked PR created as draft.
   - Lina: implement staging rollout of conservative puncturing and admin override endpoint; add safety killswitch (target 2026-09-18).
   - Samuel: add backoff heartbeat metric + composite alert; verify alert thresholds for production (target 2026-09-21).
   - Priya: run extended A/B with customer-like traces (72h) and report cost/throughput tradeoffs (target 2026-09-28).

7) Open questions / tradeoffs:
   - How aggressive should puncturing be for mixed-traffic customers? We need a per-customer policy (weighting small sequences vs throughput guarantees) rather than cluster-wide knobs.
   - Is compaction best-effort work or should it be strictly fenced off from serving worker nodes? Fencing adds cost but reduces OOM/eviction risk.

8) Communication plan for affected customers
   - Solutions eng to prepare a short note describing temporary conservative puncture rollout and that we are monitoring latency improvements. Draft by Mikhail; target 2026-09-17 for review.

Appendix - quick run commands (for oncall use)
- Check coordinator retry spike (last 30m):
  curl -s "https://metrics-api.internal/recent?metric=coalescer.coordinator.retry_rate&window=30m" | jq .
- Apply conservative puncture override (admin):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"puncture_mode":"conservative","rollout_pct":20}' https://admin.internal/coalescer/override
- Disable compaction on a node: kubectl annotate node/<node-name> coalescer.compaction=disabled && kubectl delete pod -l app=compaction-controller -n infra

Meeting notes / small decisions captured:
- We agreed to keep conservative puncturing as default for staging A until Priya's longer-run A/B completes.
- We will not immediately fence compaction off separate nodes; instead we will add compaction throttling first and measure impact.
- Kernel team will accept puncture_preference as an experimental header and keep it off by default in client SDKs unless explicitly enabled.

Next sync: 2026-09-21, focus on PR review, A/B progress, and playbook edits.

Unresolved action items to track in next sync:
- Finalize per-customer puncturing policy proposal (owner: Lina).
- Cost modeling for running puncture-heavy workloads (owner: Priya).
